# Research behind this skill

- Anthropic, [Project Swap](https://www.anthropic.com/research/project-swap), 24 September 2026. A controlled book-trading experiment involving Anthropic staff found 61% pairwise preference agreement for 188 participants who supplied rankings, compared with 50% for random guessing. In the authors' allocation comparison, inferred preferences accounted for most of the measured shortfall. This does not estimate consumer purchasing accuracy or prove that additional questions improve real outcomes. More detailed intake was associated with better agreement, without establishing causality.
- OpenAI, [Using shopping research](https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/12911370-using-shopping-research-in-chatgpt). A commercial product uses clarifying questions, optional memory and interactive feedback; this documentation describes intended behavior, not independent validation of preference accuracy.
- Google, [Agentic checkout](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/shopping/agentic-checkout-holiday-ai-shopping/), November 2025. Its announced U.S. rollout describes choosing an item, size, color and price threshold, then confirming purchase and shipping details. The narrowed task reduces the preference interpretation required at checkout; this is an inference about the design, not a reported causal result.

This skill is a proposed application of the research. Its recommendations and elicitation questions have not been independently validated. Test them against relevant real decisions and measure alignment and user effort before making claims of improvement.
